name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: First-term incumbent with no outside opposition
model.rationale: TX-26 leans heavily Republican, incumbent Brandon Gill holds a massive financial advantage, and no polls or expert ratings suggest vulnerability; markets price the race at roughly 98% Republican. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based baseline with a modest adjustment for the incumbent's resources.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected national Democratic wave could tighten the race, but nothing in the evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill, a first-term Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in a North Texas district that voted about eleven points Republican at the presidential level. He has raised over $4 million and holds more than $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Steven Shook has raised under $20,000 and has no outside support. No independent groups are spending against Gill, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Gill roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and no public general-election polling exists. With the incumbent running, well-funded, and unopposed by serious outside money, the race sits firmly in Safe Republican territory, with only a small residual chance of an upset.
